To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Resubmission of an unanswered request. I submitted the request below by email to sheriffs_recordsrequest@smcgov.org on September 13, 2026; a copy of that email is attached. I have received no acknowledgment, no determination, and no notice of extension, and the 10-day period for a determination under Gov. Code § 7922.535 has passed. I am resubmitting the request through this address so that the request and all correspondence about it are kept in one place. Please process it as the same request, as of its original submission date, and not as a new request with a new response period. Please send the overdue determination, and all further correspondence, to this address. The text below is unchanged from the original. Where it says "the date of this request," that means September 13, 2026.

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act (Gov. Code § 7920.000 et seq.), I request the following records from the San Mateo County Sheriff's Office.

This request seeks existing records only (Gov. Code § 7922.530; Sierra Club v. Superior Court (2013) 57 Cal.4th 157). Each item is limited to records created on or before the date of this request.

Scope basis. The Sheriff's Office's Memorandum of Understanding with the Northern California Regional Intelligence Center ("NCRIC"), produced by the San Mateo Police Department under Public Records Act request W012376-032026, is executed by Greg Munks, Sheriff of San Mateo County, on behalf of NCRIC. To the extent the Sheriff's Office holds, creates, or retains records in an administrative or fiscal capacity for NCRIC, those records are writings "prepared, owned, used, or retained" by the Sheriff's Office within the meaning of Gov. Code § 7920.530, regardless of whether NCRIC's day-to-day IT operations are performed by NCRIC staff, a vendor, or another member agency's personnel on NCRIC's behalf. If the Sheriff's Office takes the position that it does not hold the records described below and that some other entity is the proper respondent, please identify that entity and the basis for that position in the written determination.

As you are aware, NCRIC provided ALPR data aggregation and search services to its member agencies through a platform known as "AstroMetrics," built and operated on NCRIC's behalf by MaiVERIC, Inc. MaiVERIC's November 17, 2022 press release announcing the platform's deployment quotes Brian Rodrigues, NCRIC's Assistant Deputy Director for Information Technology & Cyber Security, and states that AstroMetrics was being provided "to 70 public safety agencies" and that it "maintains all usage records" and that "[c]lient administrators also have access to real-time data ingestion and usage logs."

As you are further aware, the vendor's own published technical documentation for the AstroMetrics platform states that NCRIC used a third-party identity provider, SecureAuth, configured to authenticate users against NCRIC's own internal Active Directory, and that users were federated into the AstroMetrics application through that mechanism — an identity realm the documentation identifies as "SecureAuth5" — rather than through any login screen operated by the vendor. That same documentation reflects that non-NCRIC personnel, including accounts associated with federal agency domains, accessed the platform through this mechanism during at least the period June through December 2023.

Civil Code § 1798.90.52 provides that an ALPR operator that accesses, or provides access to, ALPR information shall maintain a record of that access including the date and time of access, the data elements used to query the system, the username of the person accessing the information, and, as applicable, the organization or entity with which that person is affiliated, and the purpose for accessing the information. As the entity that operated AstroMetrics and provided its member agencies' and other users' access to ALPR information through that platform, NCRIC is an ALPR operator within the meaning of that section as to the records described below.

Records requested, from January 1, 2021 through the date of this request:

1. Records reflecting the population of user accounts provisioned for the AstroMetrics platform (or its predecessor or successor NCRIC ALPR aggregation platform, by whatever name), by agency or organizational affiliation — including any roster, directory export, account listing, or periodic user-count report, at any point during the period covered by this request.

2. Records describing or reflecting the process by which a person or account not affiliated with an NCRIC member agency — including any person or account affiliated with a federal agency or department — was granted an AstroMetrics account, added to NCRIC's Active Directory, or federated into AstroMetrics access through the SecureAuth identity provider or any successor identity provider.

3. Any agreement, memorandum, authorization, policy, or correspondence permitting or addressing access by any federal agency or department, or by any of its personnel or contractors, to ALPR information contributed by NCRIC member agencies, whether through AstroMetrics or any other NCRIC-operated or NCRIC-affiliated system.

4. SecureAuth or Active Directory logs, reports, or exports reflecting user account creation, modification, or deletion events, and user authentication (login) events, for the identity realm bound to the AstroMetrics application (identified in the vendor's documentation as "SecureAuth5"), for the full period such logs exist.

5. Records reflecting NCRIC's or the Sheriff's Office's access to, or possession of, the access records described in Item 1 of the request captioned "NCRIC platform access data and its disposition" submitted to the San Mateo Police Department, to the extent responsive records exist independent of anything SMPD may produce.

If no records are located for any individual item, please respond to that item separately and continue processing the remaining items.

If any portion of this request is denied, please identify the specific record withheld, state the specific statutory exemption relied upon, and produce all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions (Gov. Code §§ 7922.000, 7922.525). If any item is denied on the ground that the Sheriff's Office does not hold the responsive records in its NCRIC-administrative capacity, please identify the entity that does and the basis for that position.

Please provide the determination required by Government Code § 7922.535 within 10 days, in writing, per § 7922.540. Please acknowledge receipt of this request so the record reflects the date received.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brian Cervenka

title: Drone accident and safety event reports from public safety BVLOS waiver holders (2024–present)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Drone accident and safety event reports from public safety BVLOS waiver holders (2024–present)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

For January 1, 2024, through the date of processing:

1. All reports submitted to the FAA through FAADroneZone under Special Provision 29 of any Part 107 Certificate of Waiver and Authorization waiving 14 CFR §§ 107.31, 107.39, and 107.145 in combination (the public safety organization template issued by the Emerging Technologies Division, AFS-700, and exemplified by waiver numbers 107W-2026-01670 and 107W-2026-02013), including: (a) events reported as meeting the criteria of § 107.9 "Safety Event" reporting; (b) events in which an unmanned aircraft was operated within 500 feet vertically or horizontally of an aircraft with a person on board, including reported closest-point-of-approach distances; and (c) reported loss-of-control events.

2. All accident reports submitted under 14 CFR § 107.9 by any holder of a Part 107 Certificate of Waiver that either (a) waives exactly 14 CFR §§ 107.31, 107.39, and 107.145 (including holders of the earlier template exemplified by waiver number 107W-2025-01731), or (b) recorded "Public Safety Organization" as the Type of Operator on the waiver application. A holder meeting either condition is within the request.

3. Any flight-time record obtained by the FAA from a holder under Special Provision 25 of the template described in item 1, and any record in the Accident/Incident Data System (AIDS) or any parallel or successor sUAS dataset corresponding to the events in items 1 and 2.

4. All accident, incident, or mishap reports submitted to the FAA under any special provision or condition of a Part 91 Public Aircraft/Public Safety Operations Certificate of Waiver (waiver of 14 CFR 91.113(b) and/or 91.119), or of any Tactical BVLOS or First Responder BVLOS certificate of waiver or authorization in effect during the period.

If the FAA cannot filter items 1 through 3 by waiver instrument or Type of Operator without manual review, I will accept a complete export of all sUAS accident, safety event, and AIDS records for the period, provided the export includes every field identifying the associated waiver or certificate number, waiver template, Type of Operator, and operator name, so that operations under the named instruments can be distinguished.

Please produce records as a native database export (CSV, XLSX, or JSON) with all fields, rather than PDF images, per 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(3)(B). I do not object to redaction of individual home addresses, personal phone numbers, or personal email addresses. Operator or agency name, waiver or certificate number, date, location, aircraft make and model, injury and damage descriptions, closest-point-of-approach distances, and narrative should be released as reasonably segregable.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

HCvP

title: Obama Presidential Library: NSC Coordination and Oversight Records Regarding "Virtual Embassy Tehran" and the USAdarFarsi Farsi-Language Social Media Outreach (2011)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

NSC Coordination and Oversight Records Regarding "Virtual Embassy Tehran" and the USAdarFarsi Farsi-Language Social Media Outreach (2011)

I. Request Description & Scope

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552), I request access to and copies of historical records maintained by the Barack Obama Presidential Library within the presidential materials of the National Security Council (NSC) concerning the NSC's role in the planning, interagency coordination, and rollout of:

1. "Virtual Embassy Tehran" (iran.usembassy.gov / persian.iran.usembassy.gov), launched December 2011; and
2. The associated Farsi-language digital outreach platforms operated under the @USAdarFarsi name — the USAdarFarsi Twitter/X account, Facebook page, and any related Google+ or YouTube presence established in 2011.

Specifically, I request:

A. Policy & Action Memoranda: All Action Memorandums, Information Memorandums, Policy Guidance Memos, and Decision Memos created, received, or routed by the NSC Directorate for Iran and Persian Gulf Affairs (and/or broader Middle East Directorates) concerning the strategy, interagency approval, and public launch of Virtual Embassy Tehran and the USAdarFarsi social media accounts.

B. Interagency Coordination Records: All interagency cables, background papers, briefing materials, and meeting summaries maintained in NSC files regarding White House-level review or approval of State Department plans to establish a direct Farsi-language digital diplomatic presence aimed at Iranian audiences, January 1, 2011 – December 31, 2012.

C. Electronic Mail Communications: All emails sent, received, or copied (CC/BCC) by NSC Senior Directors, Directors, or Special Assistants for Iran and Persian Gulf Affairs containing any of the following search terms:

   - "Virtual Embassy"
   - "Tehran Embassy" AND ("virtual" OR "digital")
   - "USAdarFarsi" OR "@USAdarFarsi"
   - "iran.usembassy.gov" OR "persian.iran.usembassy.gov"

II. Targeted Record Collections & Key Custodians

To assist NARA staff in conducting an efficient search, I request that searches be prioritized within the following Presidential record collections:

- Collection: National Security Council (NSC) Records Management / Presidential Committee Materials.
- Directorate: NSC Directorate for Iran and Persian Gulf Affairs / Near East and South Asia Affairs.
- Key Officials/Custodians (including predecessor/successor roles):
  - Senior Directors for Central Region / Iran (e.g., Dennis Ross, Puneet Talwar)
  - NSC Directors for Iranian Affairs / Gulf States (2011–2012)
  - Deputy National Security Advisor for Strategic Communications (Ben Rhodes)

Note: I understand the underlying accounts were operated by the Department of State; this request is limited to NSC's oversight, coordination, and awareness of the initiative as reflected in Presidential records, not to State's own operational files.

III. Declassification of Withheld Material

I do not request that this submission be processed concurrently as a Mandatory Declassification Review (MDR) request, as I understand NARA requires an election between FOIA and MDR where the same records are at issue (36 C.F.R. § 1260.72(d)), and that MDR requires identification of specific classified material with reasonable particularity (36 C.F.R. § 1260.70(d)) — a level of specificity not yet possible for records I have not seen.

Instead, I request that if any responsive records are withheld in whole or in part under FOIA Exemption 1 (5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(1)), NARA provide a withholding log (Vaughn index) sufficiently detailed to identify each such document by date, type, and general subject. I reserve the right to submit a separate, follow-on MDR request under Section 3.5 of E.O. 13526 for the specific documents identified in that log.

IV. Fee Category

I am requesting these records as a news media requester in connection with research and reporting for MuckRock News. I authorize processing fees up to $25.00; please notify me before incurring any costs above this threshold.

V. Segregability & Response Period

As required by FOIA regulations, if any portion of a requested document is exempt from disclosure, please release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions, and cite the specific exemption(s) claimed for any material withheld in full.

Thank you for your assistance with this historical inquiry. I look forward to your acknowledgment letter.

1. Incident, problem, change, or implementation records concerning photographs that could not be retrieved, transferred, or used to complete an online driver-license renewal, including records identifying when the problem began, when it was discovered, its cause, the affected transactions, and any remediation.

2. Policies, procedures, scripts, bulletins, or other instructions to staff concerning how to handle affected customers, including whether they must appear in person, whether their online renewal payment is credited, and whether an expiring temporary license or receipt may be extended.

3. Notices, emails, letters, website messages, or other communications sent or prepared for affected customers concerning the photo problem, an incomplete renewal, a required in-person visit, or the status of their temporary document. For each form of notice, please provide existing records showing when it was used and how many customers received it, if those records exist.

4. Existing reports or exportable aggregate data showing, by week and by applicant county of residence, the number of online driver-license renewals submitted; completed; delayed, held, or rejected because a photograph was unavailable; and subsequently completed in person. Please include the applicable transaction-status and error-code definitions. If the DMV does not maintain county-level figures, please provide the statewide figures and any existing geographic breakdown. Please also provide the number of online driver-license renewal attempts during each reporting week, by applicant county of residence, so the rate of photo-related failures can be calculated using the same time period, geography, and transaction population. If the data distinguishes unique applicants from attempts or retries, please provide both counts and identify which measure is used for each status. Please include any existing county-level counts of completed online renewals and in-person renewals for the same period.

Policies, procedures, system documentation, or staff guidance concerning credits or refunds of online renewal payments and online handling fees when a customer must instead complete the renewal in person because the DMV cannot access or use the customer’s photograph. Existing aggregate reports or exportable counts showing how many customers affected by the photograph issue paid an online handling fee that was not refunded, and the total amount of those retained fees. communications.subject: Arkansas Freedom of Information Act Request: Arkansas Freedom of Information Act of 1967 Request – EPA Clean School Bus Program records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Arkansas Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request copies of the following records concerning Little Rock School District’s participation in the U.S. EPA Clean School Bus Program (CSBP) from January 1, 2022 to the present. As used below, “the provider” includes First Student (the District’s deployment contractor) and Blue Bird Body Company (the bus manufacturer):

1. Applications, award letters, and CSBP agreements naming the District, including any third-party applicant materials.
2. The District-Approval Letter for Third-Party Applicants, the School Board Awareness Certification, and any certifications or progress/status reports submitted by the provider.
3. Minutes, agendas, resolutions, and supporting meeting materials of the District’s governing board (however styled — e.g., Board of Education, Board of School Directors, Board of Trustees, or the entity’s governing authority) concerning the District’s participation in the CSBP, the authorization or approval to participate, the approval of any third-party application submitted on the District’s behalf, and the contract with the provider; and any evaluation or assessment by the District of the provider’s proposal, capacity, or ability to perform.
4. Any contracts, leases, service agreements, or lease-to-own agreements with the provider.
5. Purchase orders and invoices showing the make, model, quantity, and unit price of each bus and charger, including any Blue Bird specifications and warranty documents.
6. Delivery and acceptance records showing the date each bus was received and placed in service.
7. Operational, in-service, and service records for the CSBP buses and chargers — route or dispatch assignments; odometer or telematics/utilization data; out-of-service, downtime, and maintenance logs; and service tickets, warranty claims, recall notices, driver and mechanic reports, and complaints concerning the buses or chargers.
8. Payment Request Forms and drawdown/reimbursement records, and any records of CSBP funds returned or de-obligated.
9. Communications (including emails and attachments) concerning the CSBP buses and chargers — their procurement and orders; delivery timelines, delays, delivery, and acceptance; performance, breakdowns, and downtime; charging-infrastructure installation and operation; EPA reporting, deficiency notices, extension or workplan-revision requests, and closeout; and the drawdown, use, or return of CSBP funds.
10. All communications, proposals, presentations, and representations from the provider to the District, from before the award through the present, concerning the provider’s capacity, deployment timeline, and ability to deliver the buses and charging infrastructure, including any statements made to obtain the District’s approval or to secure or perform the award.
11. Any communications, records, or materials exchanged with First Student’s consulting or advisory personnel, however denominated (including but not limited to First Consulting and First Services), regarding the CSBP.

To speed your review and reduce your burden, I request production on a rolling basis. Please send records as they become available, beginning with whichever categories are easiest to retrieve from your systems, rather than holding everything until the full request is complete.

For the scope of this request, I rely on the statutory definition of a “public record.” Therein, "Public records" means “writings, recorded sounds, films, tapes, electronic or computer-based information, or data compilations in any medium required by law to be kept or otherwise kept and that constitute a record of the performance or lack of performance of official functions that are or should be carried out by a public official or employee, a governmental agency, or any other agency or improvement district that is wholly or partially supported by public funds or expending public funds.” Please construe this request to include email, text messages, online chats, notes, memoranda, and/or internal and external communications germane to the underlying request.

For reference, this District’s CSBP award(s) of record is as follows: 2023 Rebate — awardee First Student, Inc.: $8,625,000, 25 buses procured.

Response deadline: Records that are readily available must be made available immediately for inspection and copying. If the requested records are in active use or storage and therefore not available at the time of the request, the custodian must certify this fact in writing and set a date and hour within three (3) working days at which the records will be available. Ark. Code Ann. § 25-19-105(e). If any record is withheld or redacted, please cite each specific statutory exemption and notify me of the appeal procedures available under the law.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Sincerely,

Summer Cantone
